title: Absolute Continuity for Normed Space-Valued Functions: AC → BV
description: Answers OQ-04 from the Lebesgue FTC entry: yes, AbsolutelyContinuousOn should and can be generalized to functions f : ℝ → E for any NormedAddCommGroup E. Defines AbsolutelyContinuousOnNormed using the norm ‖·‖ in place of absolute value |·|, proves the main theorem AC_Normed → BV, and establishes that the real-valued AC is exactly the special case E = ℝ.

meta.author: Lean Genius researcher-10
meta.assumptions: None. All theorems hold for arbitrary NormedAddCommGroup E with no axioms beyond Mathlib's standard library.

mathlibDependencies.description: Additive splitting of variation over adjacent intervals — works for any PseudoEMetricSpace, including NormedAddCommGroup
Variation is zero iff function is constant on the set
Key identity: edist x y = ENNReal.ofReal ‖x - y‖ for normed groups
Commutes ofReal with finite sums of nonneg reals

originalContributions: AbsolutelyContinuousOnNormed: definition of AC for ℝ → E (any NormedAddCommGroup) using ‖·‖
normed_ac_implies_bv: proof that normed-AC implies BV, using the partition argument with edist = ENNReal.ofReal ‖·‖
lipschitz_implies_normed_ac: Lipschitz functions are normed-AC with δ = ε/(K+1)
real_ac_iff_normed_ac: the real-valued AC is exactly the E=ℝ special case
normed_ac_mono_subinterval: restriction to subintervals preserves normed-AC

openQuestions.question: Does normed-AC imply Fréchet differentiability a.e. for Banach space-valued functions? (The Lebesgue FTC would then extend to f : ℝ → E.)
Can Jordan decomposition (BV = difference of two monotone functions) be stated for normed-valued BV functions? What replaces monotone?

meta.proofStrategy: The proof of normed_ac_implies_bv mirrors the real-valued case (FundamentalTheoremCalculusLebesgueOQ01) exactly. The key substitution: the ℝ identity |x-y| = dist x y becomes the normed-space identity ‖x-y‖ = dist x y = (edist x y by ofReal). This allows the same partition argument: (1) choose n = ⌈(b-a)/δ⌉+1 pieces, (2) each piece has eVariationOn ≤ 1 by AC with ε=1, (3) inductively combine n pieces to get eVariationOn[a,b] ≤ n < ⊤.

sections.title: Definition
sections.description: AbsolutelyContinuousOnNormed: replace |f(b)-f(a)| with ‖f(b)-f(a)‖ in the ε-δ condition

sections.title: Basic Examples
sections.description: Constant functions are normed-AC; Lipschitz functions are normed-AC with δ=ε/(K+1)

sections.title: Equivalence at E=ℝ
sections.description: AbsolutelyContinuousOnNormed is equivalent to AbsolutelyContinuousOn when E=ℝ (norm = absolute value)

sections.title: Subinterval Restriction
sections.description: Normed-AC on [a,b] implies normed-AC on any subinterval [c,d]

sections.title: Main Theorem: AC → BV
sections.description: Every normed-AC function f : ℝ → E has bounded variation on [a,b]: eVariationOn f [a,b] < ⊤

content.title: Absolute Continuity for Normed Space-Valued Functions: AC → BV
content.summary: Proves that absolute continuity generalizes naturally from ℝ-valued to E-valued functions (E any NormedAddCommGroup) by replacing |·| with ‖·‖, and that this normed-AC condition implies bounded variation. The proof uses the same partition argument as the real-valued case.
content.whyMatters: Absolute continuity and bounded variation are foundational concepts in analysis. The normed-space extension is needed for: (1) vector-valued Lebesgue FTC (f : ℝ → E differentiable a.e. and ∫f' = f(b)-f(a)), (2) curves in Banach spaces (mechanics, control theory), (3) matrix-valued processes. The definition is non-trivial because the norm in E replaces the absolute value on ℝ, but the eVariationOn infrastructure in Mathlib already works for arbitrary metric spaces.
keyInsights: The key identity edist x y = ENNReal.ofReal ‖x - y‖ (for NormedAddCommGroup E) replaces the ℝ identity edist x y = ENNReal.ofReal |x - y|, making the partition proof go through identically
Mathlib's eVariationOn and BoundedVariationOn are already defined for functions to PseudoEMetricSpace (which includes NormedAddCommGroup), so no new infrastructure is needed
The real-valued AC is exactly the E=ℝ special case: |x-y| = ‖x-y‖ on ℝ
